author: SE Valley Times
title: State Rep. Carbone: 'Governor Hobbs just vetoed my bill that would root out waste, fraud, and abuse in Arizona's Medicaid program'
text:
Rep. Michael Carbone, Majority Leader (Left) & Governor Katie Hobbs (Right) | Arizona Legislature
Rep. Michael Carbone, Majority Leader (Left) & Governor Katie Hobbs (Right) | Arizona Legislature
Michael Carbone, the Majority Leader in the Arizona House, announced that Governor Katie Hobbs has vetoed his bill, HB 2449. The bill was designed to "root out waste, fraud, and abuse" in Arizona's Medicaid Program. Carbone provided his statement to the SE Valley Times.
"Governor Hobbs just vetoed my bill that would root out waste, fraud, and abuse in Arizona's Medicaid program and protect public healthcare resources for those who truly need them," said Carbone, State Representative from Arizona. "By its own estimate, the poorly named Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System has wasted over $3 billion in improper Medicaid payments since 2018, most of which is from failing to properly verify the eligibility of enrollees. My legislation would have closed loopholes that allow key eligibility factors to go unchecked during the Medicaid enrollment process and would have required more frequent eligibility checks. Governor Hobbs believes that protecting bureaucrats from additional work is more important."
According to a post on X by Arizona House Republicans, Governor Hobbs has vetoed HB 2449, a bill introduced by Carbone aimed at enhancing oversight and reducing fraud within the state's Medicaid program. The Arizona GOP said, "The Governor chose fraud and abuse." The legislation proposed measures such as cross-checking Medicaid enrollees' eligibility against state tax and lottery records and instituting more frequent eligibility verifications.
The veto occurs amid ongoing scrutiny of Arizona's Medicaid system following revelations of a $2.5 billion fraud scheme that exploited the American Indian Health Program. According to the Arizona Center for Investigative Reporting, investigations revealed that fraudulent operators billed for services not rendered, often targeting Native American communities. Despite efforts to recover lost funds, reports indicate that only about 5% has been reclaimed to date.
Carbone told the SE Valley Times: "Unfortunately, this is not the first time that Governor Hobbs has been reckless with Arizona’s Medicaid program. In 2023, it was the Republican legislature that forced the Hobbs administration to expedite the removal of hundreds of thousands of ineligible people from the Medicaid rolls, which saved Arizona taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars. My legislation would have led to even more savings."
House Bill 2449, introduced in 2025, sought to enhance the Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System's (AHCCCS) ability to verify Medicaid eligibility and reduce fraud. According to AZ Leg.gov, the bill mandated monthly data matching between AHCCCS and the Department of Revenue to identify members with lottery or gambling winnings of $3,000 or more, considering nondisclosure of such winnings a violation of eligibility terms. It also required AHCCCS to regularly review death records and out-of-state electronic benefit transactions to detect changes affecting eligibility.
Michael Carbone is a Republican member of the Arizona House of Representatives serving District 25 since January 2023 and currently holds the position of House Majority Leader.
